learningObjectives: Select and justify parallel processing in pega applications in a business scenario.
Select and justify running multiple instances of the same subprocess with a split for each shape in a business scenario.
Select and justify running multiple instances of different subprocesses with a split join shape in a business scenario.
Select and justify adding additional configuration to a subprocess in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

topics.title: Running multiple instances of the same subprocess with a Split for Each shape
Running multiple instances of different subprocesses with a Split Join shape
Adding additional configuration to a subprocess

elements.description: Independent stage processes can run concurrently. Split Join coordinates different subprocesses; Split For Each repeats one subprocess over a page list or page group. A spinoff lets the parent continue without joining back.

elements.text: Worked example: A facilities request needs a safety assessment and a budget assessment. They are different processes and can run concurrently; the parent joins after both finish.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Running multiple instances of the same subprocess with a Split for Each shape

elements.description: Use Split For Each when each eligible list/group item needs the same subprocess. Choose a join rule deliberately: All waits for every branch; Any continues after one completes and cancels remaining open assignments. Iterate processes qualifying pages sequentially.

elements.text: Worked example: A delivery has a page list of packages. Run one inspection subprocess for each package and wait for All before dispatch.

items.label: Running multiple instances of the same subprocess with a Split for Each shape

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Running multiple instances of different subprocesses with a Split Join shape

elements.description: Split Join starts different subprocesses and resumes according to All, Any or Some join criteria. Some can express a completion count or condition; do not silently assume every branch must finish.

elements.text: Worked example: Three specialist teams assess one proposal; the business needs two completed assessments. A Some join expresses the threshold.

items.label: Running multiple instances of different subprocesses with a Split Join shape

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Adding additional configuration to a subprocess

elements.description: Subprocess configuration controls the flow, page context and parameters. Review locking when branches share a case. A subprocess invoked on an embedded page must use that page's class and data rather than an unrelated top-level context.

elements.text: Worked example: An inspection flow runs on each Package page and receives an inspection-level parameter. Test that edits affect the intended package and that concurrent case saves are handled.

items.label: Adding additional configuration to a subprocess

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Repeated versus different flows
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Use Split Join merely because a list has many items.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Repeat the same flow with Split For Each.

examPitfalls.title: Spinoff is not a join
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The parent waits for a spun-off process.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use a joining shape when completion is a prerequisite.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A shipment process launches a non-blocking stock replenishment flow and must continue immediately. Which option fits?

options.text: A Wait step for replenishment completion

practiceQuiz.rationale: A spinoff does not rejoin the parent. Joining shapes and a wait would make the replenishment a completion dependency.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An application must run the same verification flow for each member of a page list. Which shape matches?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The cardinality is driven by list items while the flow stays the same. That is the Split For Each use case.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Split For Each uses Any. One branch completes. What happens to the remaining open assignments?

options.text: They all turn into spinoffs automatically
They are cancelled as the parent resumes
They must all finish before the parent resumes

practiceQuiz.rationale: Any allows the first completed branch to satisfy the join and cancels remaining open assignments. It does not mean continue while all branches remain required.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A delivery cannot proceed until every package check is complete. Which join criterion expresses this?
practiceQuiz.rationale: All makes every started subprocess a completion dependency. Any would allow the parent to continue too early.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Legal review and financial review are different flows that must run concurrently and both finish. Which configuration fits?

options.text: Split For Each with one flow name
Sequential Iterate over one embedded list

practiceQuiz.rationale: Split Join coordinates different subprocesses. All preserves the requirement that both reviews finish before continuation.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A parent may continue after two of three different assessments complete. Which join option should be considered?

options.text: Some with the required completion count

practiceQuiz.rationale: Some expresses a threshold rather than requiring all branches. The count must be configured to match the business rule.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Two parallel assignments edit the same case. Which TWO design checks are necessary?

options.text: Assume parallel flows create separate database cases automatically
Test stale-data refresh and save behavior

practiceQuiz.rationale: Parallel flow execution does not remove shared-case concurrency. Locking and stale-data handling protect the edits.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A subprocess is invoked on an embedded DeliveryItem page. What should determine its data context?

options.text: The selected step page and its class
Whichever operator opened the portal first
A new unrelated clipboard page for every property

practiceQuiz.rationale: The subprocess must operate on the intended page/class and parameters. Operator timing and ruleset versions do not select the business data page.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
